scope: Bounded current-read audit of ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.1 Table 115 CIDFont dictionary cells and the immediately consumed rules in §§9.7.3–9.7.4.3. This does not certify all CID CMaps, font programs, or §9.7.
primary_location: EC3 primary PDF Table 115 is physical pp. 345–346 / printed pp. 330–331 (table begins p.345, continues p.346; footer verified). Relevant explanatory prose: §9.7.3/Table 114 physical pp.343–345 / printed pp.328–330; §9.7.4.2 and .3 physical pp.347–349 / printed pp.332–334. Do not use the stale Table 115 locator in cid_opentype_current.

cells.source_rule: Required name; CIDFont dictionary type is Font.
cells.code: pdf-font/src/loading/opening.rs::load_composite resolves the first DescendantFonts dictionary and consumes it as the CIDFont.
cells.assertions: Deterministic public CIDFont Type2 fixtures load through Type0; no cell-isolated wrong-Type refusal asserted here.
cells.status: mapped; malformed-type refusal not claimed required

cells.source_rule: Required name: CIDFontType0 or CIDFontType2; route depends on the font program type.
cells.code: opening.rs and composite.rs branch among CFF/CID-keyed/name-keyed and TrueType CID-to-GID paths.
cells.assertions: Existing OpenType and CID mapping tests exercise representative Type0/CIDFontType2 and CIDFontType0 routes; they do not exhaust subtype/program pairings.
cells.status: representative behavior evidenced; producer pairing constraints not generalized into a rejection claim

cells.source_rule: Required name. The name identifies the font and may contain the standard six-uppercase-letter subset prefix when embedded subsetted programs are used.
cells.code: Font opening/substitution and program identity paths use BaseFont/descriptor names.
cells.assertions: Existing embedded composite fixtures use matching LiberationSans names; no claim of exhaustive subset-name parsing from this cell review.

cells.source_rule: Required dictionary with Registry, Ordering, Supplement as Table 114 specifies. For non-Identity CMaps, Registry and Ordering of CMap and CIDFont are to match; Supplement is not the compatibility key. Identity CMaps are compatible with any CIDFont. #518 separately permits an array in CMap CIDSystemInfo; it is not a Table 115 CIDFont cell change.
cells.code: composite.rs::collection_table, collection_gap and composite_cmap route collection identity and fallback.
cells.assertions: composite.rs tests cover missing/malformed collection identity and representative substitution; `cid_opentype_current` maps predefined and identity cases. No full Registry/Ordering compatibility matrix was demonstrated in this cell pass.

cells.source_rule: Required dictionary. EC3 #106 strikes the Table 115 words requiring an indirect reference; a direct dictionary is therefore permitted. Descriptor entries then follow Table 120 plus applicable CIDFont descriptor additions in Table 122.
cells.code: opening.rs::load_composite uses Document::get_key(descendant, "FontDescriptor") and accepts the resolved object when it is a dictionary; embedded_program then resolves FontFile2/FontFile3 data.
cells.assertions: Current deterministic embedded CIDFont fixtures use an indirect descriptor object. Existing inline direct descriptors elsewhere test simple-font/unit paths, not an embedded public CIDFont consumer.
cells.status: specific evidence gap; focused direct-descriptor integration draft supplied

cells.source_rule: Optional number; default width 1000 glyph-space units. §9.7.4.3 constrains stated W/DW to be consistent with the font program.
cells.code: metrics.rs::composite_widths reads W/DW for CID advances.
cells.assertions: composite_font_fixtures.rs::the_w_array_of_example_1_states_each_width covers explicit W forms; other source example assertions cover DW/default behavior. `indirect_function_colour_current` is unrelated.
cells.status: literal API controls exist; no pixel claim added

cells.source_rule: Optional array of per-CID widths in either of the two §9.7.4.3 forms; DW applies where no W entry states a width. If a CID is specified more than once, the first specification is used.
cells.code: metrics.rs::composite_widths parses both forms and resolves entries.
cells.assertions: composite_font_fixtures.rs::the_w_array_of_example_1_states_each_width asserts the standard's sample widths and duplicate-first behavior; cid_map_stream_spec_audit.rs has a public embedded-font metric/render route.
cells.status: strong selected syntax/metric evidence; forms and unrelated cases not exhaustively certified

cells.source_rule: Vertical writing only; optional two-number array, default [880 -1000] glyph-space units. CMap writing mode selects vertical metrics.
cells.code: metrics.rs::Vertical::read and loading/advances.rs use DW2 only when vertical mode is selected.
cells.assertions: composite_font_fixtures.rs::dw2_of_example_2_places_a_glyph_no_w2_entry_names checks default and explicit values; vertical placement tests exist, but this feature row is primarily API-level numeric evidence.
cells.status: selected defaults/values evidenced; producer restriction is not treated as reader rejection duty

cells.source_rule: Vertical writing only; optional array using per-CID triplets in the two §9.7.4.3 forms; DW2 fills unspecified CIDs.
cells.assertions: composite_font_fixtures.rs::the_w2_array_of_example_3_states_each_vertical_metric checks source example triplets; public vertical corpus tests are optional and can skip.
cells.status: selected syntax/value evidence; no complete vertical-placement certification

cells.source_rule: For CIDFontType2, type is stream or name; when a name is used it shall be Identity. Table 115 marks the map required specifically for Type2 CIDFonts with embedded font programs. If a stream lacks the requested GID, §9.7.6.3 directs fallback to CID 0's glyph. The map stream encodes two-byte GID values, high-order byte first. §9.7.4.2 says to ignore it for a substituted font.
cells.code: composite.rs::cid_to_glyph; opening.rs::load_composite deliberately avoids using it in the substituted route.
cells.assertions: Tracked crates/pdf-model/tests/cid_map_stream_spec_audit.rs exercises exact-xref CID5->GID37 big-endian selection, short-map CID6->CID0/GID36 fallback, two real outlines, and complete public interpretation. The draft in cid_opentype_current was promoted; historical wave log is not a fresh run claim.
cells.status: strong targeted assertion; not all map lengths or font program formats certified

cells.conditions: Table115's FontDescriptor and CIDSystemInfo producer requirements are not used alone to infer a mandatory reader rejection behavior. Table115's stream/name restrictions are source rules, but absent malformed-input tests are not recorded as failures. Table 119 is the distinct Type0 outer dictionary; do not conflate its DescendantFonts constraints with these descendant CIDFont cells.

No independent public embedded-CIDFont consumer assertion currently isolates a direct /FontDescriptor dictionary after #106. The scratch draft does.
